question: A train covers a distance of 270 km in 4.5 hours. What is the speed of the train?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula: Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Convert 4.5 hours to a fraction: 4.5 = 9/2 hours.

Speed = 270 ÷ (9/2) = 270 × (2/9)

Speed = 30 × 2 = 60 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 60 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
• 
 
 
 Start
 End
 
 

 Distance = 270 km
 
 
 Time = 4.5 hours
 
 
 
 
 Speed = ?

**Given:**

Distance covered by the train = 270 km

Time taken = 4.5 hours

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Speed = 270 ÷ 4.5

⇒ Speed = 2700 ÷ 45

⇒ Speed = 60 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 60 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance Covered ÷ Total Time Taken. If a person covers two equal distances at speeds x and y, Average Speed = (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

When two bodies move in the same direction, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. When moving in opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.
